failure_summary.description: Returned only one component of a canonical proper name instead of the full named entity.
Over-synthesized alternatives or inferred an answer relation from an underspecified elliptical prompt.
Expanded people’s names beyond the concise form expected by the clue or answer source.
Missed the requested referent despite existing guidance: gave the altered title instead of the Shakespeare title, and a description instead of the named object.

patch.reasoning: The people-name guidance currently favors retaining every supported name element, which can conflict with a clue’s conventional short form or a directly paired answer label. Add a distinction for completing a named entity in a fragment, and for choosing a principal answer rather than combining exceptions. The title-relation and formula failures already contradict explicit rules, so duplicating those rules is unlikely to help.

edits.target: For people, use the full identity supported by substantive context; do not answer with only a surname merely because a clue echo abbreviates it. Preserve initials, titles, and other name elements when the clue or a reliable passage supplies them—do not strip them for stylistic normalization.
edits.content: For people, use the name form appropriate to the clue and the requested scope. When a reliable passage directly pairs the exact clue with an answer label, reproduce that label, even if it uses a surname alone. Otherwise use the conventional public name at the level needed to identify the person: retain distinguishing initials or other elements when needed, but do not add optional middle initials or expand a familiar name solely because they appear in background sources.

## Complete Named Entities in Clue Fragments
When a clue uses a blank inside the conventional name of an entity, determine whether it asks you to identify the entity or explicitly to supply only the missing word. For an entity-identification clue, return the full conventional name, not just one component of it; give only the missing token when the wording specifically requests that token.

When a question seeks a conventional answer and the evidence distinguishes a principal or usual source from occasional alternatives, return the principal answer rather than combining all listed possibilities. Enumerate alternatives only when the question asks for a complete list.
